mainTopic: פיקוח נפש on שבת: saving a person in doubt (the abandoned baby and the rockslide victim), how we check for life, and the source that saving a life overrides שבת.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of a תינוק מושלך (an abandoned baby) found in a city of Jews and non-Jews. The גמרא shows that שמואל was being lenient: even where most people are non-Jews, we break שבת to dig the baby out, because we do not follow the majority when a life is at stake. It then explains what each status of the baby affects. A non-Jewish majority affects feeding him נבלות, a Jewish majority affects returning his lost objects, and a half-and-half city affects נזקין. Next the גמרא explains the משנה of the מפולת (rockslide). It builds up from one doubt to two, and teaches that we dig even for חיי שעה. The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say 'if dead, leave him'. It tries to answer from רבי יהודה בן לקיש, then rejects that answer. A ברייתא then discusses how far we dig to check for life, the nose or the heart, and רב פפא limits that מחלוקת. Finally, sages on the road are asked for the source that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת. רבי ישמעאל gives a קל וחומר from the thief breaking in. רבי עקיבא begins a proof from a murderer at the מזבח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל seems to apply the majority rule to saving a life
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed by citing שמואל, who seems to say the clause is about digging the baby out from under rubble on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: the teaching is about removing the rubble from on top of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge. It quotes שמואל, who seems to say the majority rule decides whether we may dig the baby out on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל means 'when most are non-Jews, he is a non-Jew, so we do not dig him out,' then he is following the majority even when a life is at stake. That contradicts the rule that we do not follow the majority in פיקוח נפש.

keyTerms.meaning: to clear away or remove, here meaning to dig out
a heap of rubble or debris
saving a life, which overrides שבת

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This continues the challenge raised on the previous amud.

phrases.english: [The teaching is] about removing the rubble from on top of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר לְפַקֵּחַ עָלָיו אֶת הַגַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that we do not follow the majority in פיקוח נפש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read plainly, שמואל connects the majority rule to whether we dig the baby out on שבת. That would mean a majority of non-Jews could stop us from saving him.

steps.title: שמואל's statement was on the first clause and was a leniency
steps.stepSummary: שמואל was commenting on the first clause, and he meant that for saving a life the majority rule does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל's statement was said, it was said on the first clause: 'If most are non-Jews, he is a non-Jew.' שמואל said: But regarding saving a life, it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It reframes שמואל's statement as a leniency: even when most are non-Jews, we still dig the baby out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed שמואל was using the majority to decide when we may dig. In fact he limited the majority rule. 'He is a non-Jew' holds for other laws, but not for פיקוח נפש, where any doubt is enough to save him.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (a statement of an אמורא)

steps.whatToRemember: Even in a city where most people are non-Jews, we break שבת to save an abandoned baby. We do not follow the majority when a life is at stake.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'לפקח עליו את הגל' do not mean שמואל forbids digging when most are non-Jews. He is saying the reverse: the 'non-Jew' status does not stop us from saving him.

phrases.english: When [the statement] of Shmuel was said,
it was said on the first clause:
'If most are non-Jews, he is a non-Jew.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וּלְעִנְיַן פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ אֵינוֹ כֵּן.
phrases.english: Shmuel said: But regarding saving a life, it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-placing the statement: it applies to a different clause than assumed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל was using the majority to decide whether to dig the baby out.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל commented on the first clause to exclude פיקוח נפש from the majority rule.

steps.title: What law does 'majority non-Jews' affect?
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'non-Jew' status does not affect saving his life, the גמרא asks what it does affect.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If most are non-Jews, he is a non-Jew.' For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section that goes through each clause of the teaching. It asks what practical difference the first clause makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that this status does not stop us from saving him. So the גמרא wants to know where the status actually matters.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? (what practical difference does it make?)

phrases.english: If most are non-Jews, he is a non-Jew.
For what law [does this matter]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2: since it is not about saving his life, what is it about?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law that follows from treating the baby as a non-Jew.

steps.title: רב פפא: we may feed him non-kosher food
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the 'non-Jew' status allows feeding the baby נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: To feed him non-kosher meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the clause means we may feed the baby food that is forbidden to Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because we assume he is a non-Jew, we do not have to keep him away from איסורים. We may feed him נבלות.

keyTerms.meaning: meat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
To feed him non-kosher meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3.

steps.title: What law does 'majority Jews' affect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the second clause makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If most are Jews, he is a Jew.' For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second clause and asks the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many laws are stricter, such as saving his life, and those already apply even when we are in doubt. So the גמרא looks for a law where we need to actually treat him as a Jew.

phrases.english: If most are Jews, he is a Jew.
For what law [does this matter]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַאי הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the next clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law that follows from treating the baby as a Jew.

steps.title: We must return his lost objects
steps.stepSummary: Because he is treated as a Jew, there is a duty of השבת אבידה toward him.
steps.simpleTranslation: To return his lost object to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we must return his lost items, just as we would for any Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of השבת אבידה applies to a fellow Jew. The majority makes him count as a Jew for this obligation.

phrases.english: To return his lost object to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The duty of השבת אבידה applies to him.

steps.title: What law does 'half and half' affect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the third clause makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Half and half, he is a Jew.' For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last clause, where the city is evenly split, and asks the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no majority, the baby's status is a true doubt. Even so, the teaching says he is a Jew, so the גמרא asks where that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: half and half, an even split

phrases.english: Half and half, he is a Jew.
For what law [does this matter]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַאי הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the third clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law the 'Jew' status in a half-and-half city affects.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it is about damages
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the third clause is about laws of נזקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: For damages.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers that the clause matters for damages cases. The גמרא will now ask which case exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damages between a Jew and a non-Jew are paid differently than damages between two Jews. So the baby's status changes how much is paid.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: For damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The status matters for laws of damages.

steps.title: If a Jew's ox gored his ox, he would need proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the damages case is. It rejects the case where he is the one claiming money, since a claimant must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say our ox gored his ox, let him bring proof [that he is a Jew] and then take!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the damages case could be. It shows that one possible case cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is the damaged party, he is asking for money. The rule is המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה: whoever wants to take money must prove his claim. Since his status is in doubt, a doubtful 'Jew' status cannot win him money.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that it gored
our ox [gored] his ox,
let him bring proof and take!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests ריש לקיש's answer by searching for a case that works.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the 'Jew' status matters for damages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When he is the claimant, the burden of proof is on him. A doubtful status cannot help him collect, so the status makes no difference in that case.

steps.title: The case is where his ox gored a Jew's ox
steps.stepSummary: The status matters when he is the one paying. He pays half like a Jew, and the other side must prove he is not a Jew to collect more.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where his ox gored our ox. Half he gives him. For the other half he can say: 'Bring proof that I am not a Jew, and take.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case where the baby, now grown, is the one who must pay. Here his doubtful status protects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew whose ox is a שור תם pays half damages. A non-Jew's ox pays in full. He pays the half that is certain. For the other half, the damaged party is the one trying to take money, so he must prove the baby is a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a case where)

steps.whatToRemember: In a half-and-half city, 'he is a Jew' means he gets the benefit of the doubt when he is the one paying. The other side must prove he is a non-Jew.
steps.confusionAlert: 'He is a Jew' in the half-and-half case does not mean he is certainly Jewish. It only means he can hold on to his money, because the claimant carries the burden of proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a status in doubt helps the person holding the money but never helps the person claiming it, a basic principle of monetary law.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where his ox gored our ox.
Half he gives him;
phrases.notes: This is what a Jew pays for a שור תם.

phrases.english: for the other half, he can say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתִי רְאָיָה דְּלָאו יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנָא וּשְׁקוֹל.
phrases.english: 'Bring proof that I am not a Jew, and take.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּנַגְחֵיהּ תּוֹרָא דִּידֵיהּ לְתוֹרָא דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by switching which side is paying.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: he is the defendant, not the claimant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The damages case is one where he is collecting money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where he is paying. His doubtful 'Jew' status lets him pay only half unless the damaged party proves he is a non-Jew.

steps.title: What is the משנה's list of doubts trying to say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a person trapped under a מפולת and asks what its list of three doubts is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Someone on whom a rockslide fell, etc.' What is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks a question about it. This sets up the next step, which explains the משנה's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three doubts: maybe he is there or not, maybe he is alive or dead, maybe he is a גוי or a Jew. The גמרא wants to know why all three are needed. It also wants to know what point the list is building toward.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.': the quote continues past these words
'What is it saying?': a request to explain the meaning or structure of a text

phrases.english: One upon whom a rockslide fell, etc.
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה. The earlier discussion of נזקין and a person's status is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה list three separate doubts, and how do they fit together?

steps.title: The משנה builds up from easy doubts to harder ones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is written in a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Each doubt is a bigger חידוש than the one before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying 'needless to say.' Needless to say, if we are unsure whether he is there or not, we clear the rubble, because if he is there he is alive. But even if we are unsure whether he is alive or dead, we clear it. And needless to say, if we are unsure whether he is alive or dead but he is a Jew, we clear it. But even if we are unsure whether he is a גוי or a Jew, we clear it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה climbs step by step. Each doubt is more surprising than the last, and we still clear the rubble on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first doubt, if he is there at all, he is surely alive, so clearing is clearly worth it. In the second, he may already be dead, and still we clear. In the third, he may not even be a Jew, and still we clear. This shows that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת even when two doubts are stacked together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Needless to say': a style that moves from the obvious case to the bigger חידוש
We clear away the rubble (even on שבת)
Saving a life, which overrides שבת

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת we clear rubble for someone who might be there, might be alive, and might be a Jew. Even layered doubts about saving a life override שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: In a 'לא מיבעיא' list, the first case is the easiest, not the main חידוש. The real חידוש is the last and hardest case.

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'needless to say':

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם,
phrases.english: Needless to say, when it is uncertain whether he is there or not there,
since if he is there, he is alive, so we clear the rubble,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ סָפֵק חַי סָפֵק מֵת — מְפַקְּחִין.
phrases.english: but even if it is uncertain whether he is alive or dead, we clear.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא סָפֵק חַי סָפֵק מֵת, דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: And needless to say, when uncertain alive or dead, if he is a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ סָפֵק גּוֹי סָפֵק יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְפַקְּחִין.
phrases.english: but even if it is uncertain whether he is a gentile or a Jew, we clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three doubts form a 'לא מיבעיא' build-up. Each is a bigger חידוש, and in all of them we violate שבת to clear the rubble.

steps.title: Why say 'if found alive, keep clearing'? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'if found alive, we clear' and asks why it needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If they found him alive, they clear the rubble.' If they found him alive, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a line of the משנה as unnecessary. Of course you keep digging out a living person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already taught that we clear even when it is doubtful whether he is alive. So when he is surely alive, clearing seems obvious. The גמרא asks what new point this line adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious!': a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new

phrases.english: If they found him alive, they clear the rubble.
If they found him alive, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and challenges it as obvious.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we clear rubble even when it is doubtful he is alive, clearing for someone surely alive teaches nothing new.

steps.title: We clear even if he will only live a short time
steps.stepSummary: The line teaches that we violate שבת even when the person will only live a short while (חיי שעה).
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed to teach that we clear even for a short time of life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's line is not obvious. It teaches that we dig him out even if he will soon die anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think breaking שבת is only allowed to save a person for the long term. The משנה teaches that even a few extra moments of life are worth violating שבת. This is the חידוש of חיי שעה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for…': introduces the case where the statement teaches something new
A short time of life; someone who will live only briefly

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major source that saving even חיי שעה overrides שבת. It is a basic rule in the הלכות of פיקוח נפש.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary: that even for a short time of life we clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the line in a narrower, non-obvious case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think we only violate שבת for someone who will survive for the long term.
steps.terutzMaskana: We clear the rubble even if he will live only a short time (חיי שעה).

steps.title: Why say 'if dead, leave him'? That is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'if dead, leave him' and asks why it needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if he is dead, they should leave him.' Isn't this also obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges another line of the משנה as unnecessary. Why would anyone break שבת for a dead body?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We break שבת only to save a life, and a dead person cannot be saved. So the instruction to leave the body seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: They should leave him (where he is)
'This too': the same challenge applied again

phrases.english: And if he is dead, they should leave him.
Isn't this also obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'פשיטא' challenge on the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no life to save, so it is obvious that we may not break שבת for a dead body.

steps.title: Needed because of רבי יהודה בן לקיש, who allows saving a body from a fire
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed because a ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה בן לקיש as allowing a dead body to be rescued from a fire on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed because of רבי יהודה בן לקיש. As a ברייתא teaches: We do not rescue a dead body from a fire. רבי יהודה בן לקיש said: I heard that we do rescue a dead body from a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we might have thought a dead body may be moved on שבת. There is an opinion that allows saving a body from a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual view is that we may not break שבת to save a dead body from a fire. רבי יהודה בן לקיש holds that we may. From his view, one might also allow clearing rubble off a body, so the משנה must say 'leave him.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'As was taught in a ברייתא': brings a source from outside the משנה
'I heard': passing on a received tradition

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: No, it is necessary according to Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין מַצִּילִין אֶת הַמֵּת מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה,
phrases.english: As it was taught: One may not save a corpse from a fire.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּצִּילִין אֶת הַמֵּת מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה.
phrases.english: I heard that one may save a corpse from a fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 15 by pointing to a contrary opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the line is not obvious, because a known opinion permits moving a body on שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבי יהודה בן לקיש, one might think we may clear rubble off a dead body on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that a dead body under rubble is left there.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה בן לקיש agrees for a rockslide
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן לקיש allowed saving a body from a fire only so that a panicked relative would not put out the fire. A rockslide carries no such danger, so even he agrees we leave the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יהודה בן לקיש only said this because a person is frantic over his dead relative. If you do not allow him to take the body, he will come to put out the fire. But here, if you do not allow him, what could he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יהודה בן לקיש's ruling. It then shows that this reason does not apply to a body under rubble. This undercuts the answer of step 16: even according to רבי יהודה בן לקיש, the line 'if dead, leave him' would be obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His leniency was not about honoring the dead. It was about preventing a worse sin: a frantic relative might put out the fire, which is a serious איסור דאורייתא. Under rubble there is no greater sin to fear, so the משנה's ruling holds even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Frantic and panicked over his dead relative
'What can he do?': there is nothing worse he could come to do

steps.whatToRemember: We do not break שבת for a dead body under rubble. Even רבי יהודה בן לקיש, who allowed saving a body from a fire, did so only to keep a panicked relative from putting out the fire.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה בן לקיש does not hold that honoring the dead overrides שבת. His leniency is only a safeguard against the bigger איסור of extinguishing.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ לָא קָאָמַר
phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish said this only

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁאָדָם בָּהוּל עַל מֵתוֹ,
phrases.english: because a person is frantic over his dead relative;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ — אָתֵי לְכַבּוֹיֵי.
phrases.english: if you do not permit him, he will come to extinguish the fire.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, אִי לָא שָׁרֵית לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: But here, if you do not permit him,
what could he do?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the opinion cited in step 16 and shows it does not apply to a rockslide, so step 16's answer is rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A dead body under rubble is left there on שבת. רבי יהודה בן לקיש's fire leniency was only to prevent extinguishing, and that concern does not exist in a rockslide.

steps.title: How far do we dig to check for life: the nose or the heart?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. One opinion says we check up to the nose. The יש אומרים say we check up to the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Up to where does he check? Up to his nose. Some say: up to his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a person buried under a collapse on שבת. It asks how much of the body we must uncover to find out whether he is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'if alive, clear; if dead, leave,' but it never said how we find out. One view says breathing at the nose is the test. The יש אומרים say we must reach the heart to check for a heartbeat.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question of how far we may dig to save him. If he is found alive, we dig him out completely. The question is only how far we must dig to find out whether he is still alive.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Up to where does he check?
phrases.notes: That is, how far does he uncover the buried person to see if he is alive.

phrases.english: Up to his nose.
And some say: up to his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד הֵיכָן הוּא בּוֹדֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether we dig to how we determine life or death, which is the practical side of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first view says checking up to the nose is enough. The יש אומרים require checking up to the heart.

steps.title: Do not assume the lower victims are dead
steps.stepSummary: If the top victims are found dead, we may not assume the lower ones are dead too. There was a real case where the lower ones were alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he checked and found the upper ones dead, he should not say, 'The lower ones have already died.' It once happened that they found the upper ones dead and the lower ones alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a rule for a collapse that buries several people. Finding dead people on top does not allow us to stop digging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that if the people on top died, the people underneath surely died too, so there is no reason to keep digging on שבת. The ברייתא rejects this guess. It backs up its rule with a real event where the lower people survived.

keyTerms.meaning: there was an incident (a real case)

steps.whyThisMatters: In פיקוח נפש we do not stop based on a likely guess. We keep breaking שבת as long as there is a real chance that someone is alive.

phrases.english: If he checked and found the upper ones dead,
he should not say: The lower ones have already died.
There was an incident
and they found the upper ones dead and the lower ones alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a further rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Finding the upper victims dead does not allow us to stop digging for the lower ones.

steps.title: Is this the same as the מחלוקת about where a baby begins to form?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the nose/heart מחלוקת matches a מחלוקת about whether a fetus begins forming from the head or from the navel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say these תנאים argue like those תנאים? As it was taught: From where does a fetus begin to form? From its head, as it says, 'From my mother's womb You are גוזי,' and it says, 'Cut off (גזי) your hair and throw it away.' אבא שאול says: from its navel, and it sends out its roots in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that our מחלוקת is really one already known from another ברייתא. This is a suggestion only, and the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is this: wherever life begins is where life is mainly found. Whoever says a baby forms from the head would check the nose, which is in the head. אבא שאול says a baby forms from the navel, which is the middle of the body, so he would check the heart. The verses connect the word גוזי to cutting hair, which hints at the head.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say (introduces a proposed suggestion)
these תנאים argue like those תנאים
a תנא who says the fetus forms from the navel

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי.
phrases.english: Shall we say these Tannaim argue like those Tannaim?
As it was taught: From where is the fetus formed?
From its head,
as it says: 'From my mother's womb You are the One who took me out (gozi)',
and it says: 'Cut off (gozi) your hair and throw it away.'
phrases.notes: ירמיה ז:כט. The shared word links forming to hair, which means the head.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says: From its navel,
and it sends out its roots in every direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to tie the מחלוקת in the ברייתא to an existing מחלוקת about where a fetus forms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the nose/heart מחלוקת the same as the head/navel מחלוקת about fetal formation?

steps.title: No link: even אבא שאול agrees life is shown in the nose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. אבא שאול spoke only about how a body forms. For saving a life, he agrees the main sign of life is in the nose.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows אבא שאול. He only spoke there about forming, since everything forms from its middle. But for saving a life, even אבא שאול agrees that life is mainly in the nose, as it is written: 'All that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion from the previous step. Our מחלוקת does not depend on the one about fetal formation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where a body begins to grow is one question. Where we see the clearest sign of life is a different question. אבא שאול's view on growth from the middle does not force him to check the heart. The פסוק about the מבול shows that life is identified by breath in the nose.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say (introduces a rejection)
he only said this far (limits a view to its own case)

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Abba Shaul;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל הָתָם
phrases.english: Abba Shaul only said there
regarding formation,
since everything is formed from its middle;
but regarding saving a life,
even Abba Shaul agrees
that the main sign of life is in the nose,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כׇּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'All that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed link between the two מחלוקות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the nose/heart מחלוקת depends on the fetal-formation מחלוקת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion mixed up where the body begins to grow with where life is identified. These are two separate questions.

steps.title: רב פפא: the מחלוקת applies only when digging from the feet up
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits the מחלוקת to digging from the bottom up. If we dig from the top down, checking the nose is enough for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The מחלוקת is when digging from below upward. But from above downward, once he has checked up to the nose, he does not need to check further, as it is written: 'All that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains exactly when the two opinions in the ברייתא disagree. He also gives the rule that everyone accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging from the feet up, you reach the heart before the nose. That is where the views split: is the heart check enough, or must you keep digging to the nose? Digging from the head down, you reach the nose first, and no breath there is enough for everyone to say he is dead, based on the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who limits the scope of the מחלוקת

steps.whatToRemember: The nose (breathing) is the decisive sign of life. If you dig from the head down and find no breath at the nose, you may stop. The ברייתא's מחלוקת applies only when digging from the feet up.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the יש אומרים always require checking the heart. רב פפא says that when digging from the head down, everyone agrees the nose is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The dispute is when digging from below upward;
but from above downward,
once he has checked him up to his nose,
he no longer needs to check further,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'All that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַחְלוֹקֶת מִמַּטָּה לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 18 and defines when its מחלוקת applies, using the same פסוק as step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When digging from the head down, checking the nose is enough for everyone. The מחלוקת exists only when digging from the feet up.

steps.title: The sages on the road are asked for the source that saving a life overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה were walking, with two younger scholars behind them. Someone asked them for the Torah source that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה were walking on the road. לוי הסדר and רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה were walking behind them. This question was asked in front of them: Where do we learn that saving a life overrides שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section with a story. It sets up a question, and the answers from the sages come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא took for granted that we dig through rubble on שבת to save a life. Now it asks for the actual Torah source behind that rule. The question is not whether the rule is true. It asks where we learn it.

keyTerms.meaning: Saving a life (literally 'uncovering a soul', as in clearing rubble off a person)
From where do we know? (asking for a source)
'The arranger', a title of לוי, who organized teachings

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody in the story doubts that saving a life overrides שבת. They are only looking for the verse or reasoning it comes from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source discussion for the basic הלכה that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.

phrases.english: It once happened that Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: and Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
were walking on the road,
and Levi HaSadar

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
were walking behind them.
phrases.notes: They walked behind out of respect for their teachers.

phrases.english: This question was asked before them:
From where do we know that saving a life
overrides Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין לְפִקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁדּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of digging out victims on שבת (steps 18-22) to the basic source of the rule itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that פיקוח נפש overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר from the thief breaking in
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reasons from the thief found in a tunnel. A homeowner may kill him even though we are unsure whether he came for money or for lives. So saving a life certainly overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל answered: The Torah says, 'If a thief is found breaking in.' We are not sure whether this thief came only for money or also to kill. Killing is so severe that it makes the land impure and drives the שכינה away from Israel. Even so, the homeowner may save himself by taking the thief's life. All the more so, saving a life overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives his answer to the question using a קל וחומר (an 'all the more so' argument).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing a person is far more serious than breaking שבת. Yet the Torah allows it even when the danger is only a doubt, since the thief may have come only for money. If a mere doubt about danger permits something as severe as killing, it surely permits breaking שבת to save a life.

keyTerms.meaning: A tunnel or break-in, where a thief digs into a house
An 'all the more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof is built on doubt. That teaches that even a possible danger to life is enough to override שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael answered and said:
"If a thief is found breaking in"
phrases.notes: שמות כב:א. The homeowner who kills him is not guilty.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה זֶה, שֶׁסָּפֵק עַל מָמוֹן בָּא
phrases.english: Now if this one, where it is uncertain whether he comes for money
or uncertain whether he comes for lives,
and bloodshed makes the land impure,
and causes the Divine Presence to leave Israel,
yet one may save himself at the cost of the thief's life,
then all the more so, saving a life
overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question asked in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: if even severe bloodshed is permitted out of a doubtful threat to life, then breaking שבת is surely permitted to save a life.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא begins: a murderer is taken from beside the altar, not from on top of it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא quotes the verse about a deliberate murderer: 'from My altar you shall take him to die.' He reads it as 'from beside My altar' (before starting the service), but not 'from on top of My altar' (in the middle of the service).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא answered: The Torah says, 'If a man acts deliberately against his neighbor… from My altar you shall take him to die.' 'From My altar' means from beside it, but not from on top of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא starts a different proof. Here he only sets up his source, a reading of a verse about a כהן who is a murderer. The point about saving a life comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'מעם מזבחי' teaches two cases. If a murderer כהן is about to begin the עבודה, we take him away for execution. If he is already standing on the מזבח doing the עבודה, we let him finish. So the עבודה in the מקדש is important enough to delay an execution.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From with My altar', from beside the altar
'From on top of My altar', in the middle of the service

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect שבת in this step yet. רבי עקיבא is laying groundwork about the מזבח. He connects it to saving a life only after the next statements.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva answered and said:
"And if a man acts deliberately against his neighbor, etc.
from My altar you shall take him, to die."
"From My altar":
phrases.notes: From beside it, before he begins the service.

phrases.english: but not from on top of My altar.
phrases.notes: If he is in the middle of the service, he is allowed to finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 23, alongside רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins a derivation from the verse of a murderer at the מזבח. The completed proof continues next.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the rule: not removing him from the altar applies only for execution
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. The rule that we do not take a כהן down from the מזבח applies only when we want to execute him. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this rule (that we do not take him off the מזבח) when the goal is to put him to death…
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא's statement is brought into רבי עקיבא's proof to limit the rule about the מזבח. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא שנו אלא' narrow the rule to execution only. This sets up a contrast with a different purpose, which the גמרא completes next. רבי עקיבא will build his proof for פיקוח נפש from that contrast.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught…', a phrase that limits a rule to a narrow case
To put to death, to execute

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only regarding taking him to execute him,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְהָמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule from step 25 ('not from on top of My altar') as part of building רבי עקיבא's proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that a כהן is not taken down from the מזבח applies only when the purpose is to execute him. The rest of the statement follows on the next amud.
